about.title: Dos Palos Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Dos Palos sits in Merced County, where agriculture, trucking, and small commercial operations along Rt 33 and Elgin Avenue keep plenty of workers on the move. When a job injury happens here, the first question is usually about workers' compensation. But comp isn't always the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on SR-33 contributed to what happened, you may have a separate injury claim against that third party, on top of any comp benefits. Local crash data shows Dos Palos sees a handful of injury collisions each year, some involving people simply driving for work. Whether you were hurt operating farm machinery, working a delivery route, or on a job site, understanding your options matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can look at your specific situation and explain what applies.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Dos Palos Work Injury

items.title: Comp Isn't Always the Full Picture
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party, like a subcontractor or equipment maker, can still be held separately liable. An attorney can help identify whether that applies to you.

items.title: Deadlines Work Differently Depending on the Claim
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, while a third-party injury claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.title: Retaliation for Reporting Is Illegal
items.desc: California law protects you from being punished for reporting a workplace injury. If you're worried about your job while dealing with a claim, an attorney can explain your protections.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work near Frank Avenue. Does workers' comp cover that?
items.answer: Possibly, since injuries while driving for work duties are often covered by comp. But if another driver caused the collision, you may also have a separate claim against that driver. An attorney can review the details and explain both paths.

items.question: Can I still file a claim if my employer says it was my fault?
items.answer: Yes. California workers' comp generally doesn't require proving fault, since it's a no-fault system for employer claims. Fault becomes more relevant only in a third-party claim, which is a separate matter entirely.

items.question: What if I'm afraid my employer will retaliate if I report an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a legitimate workplace injury is illegal under California law. If you're concerned about your job, an independent attorney can walk you through your rights before you file anything.
